questions: Q1: What CLI structure changes are needed for hlx inspect netsuite and hlx run?
Q2: How should --env parameter be passed to the server endpoints?
Q3: Should hlx run be a top-level command or under inspect?

answers.answer: Two new handler files (src/inspect/netsuite.ts and src/run/index.ts) following the existing db.ts pattern: resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST /{repoId}/{type} -> console.log JSON. Two modified files: src/inspect/index.ts adds case 'netsuite' to the switch, src/index.ts adds case 'run' to the main dispatcher. Both use the existing hxFetch client with default basePath /api/inspect. No new dependencies.
evidence: src/inspect/db.ts:1-12 — Template: resolveRepo, hxFetch POST /{repoId}/database, console.log JSON. 12 lines.
src/inspect/index.ts:41-128 — Inspect router switch with repos/db/logs/api cases. Add netsuite after api.
src/index.ts:81-156 — Main dispatcher switch with 13 commands. Add run after existing commands.
src/lib/http.ts:43 — Default basePath '/api/inspect'. No override needed.

answers.answer: The --env parameter is parsed via getFlag(args, '--env') and included in the hxFetch POST body as { env: 'prod' | 'sandbox' }. When --env is not provided by the user, the CLI reads nsDefaultEnv from the manifest (/tmp/helix-inspect/manifest.json) and sends that instead. This matches how --limit is passed in the logs handler (body parameter). The server handler maps 'prod' -> PRODUCTION, 'sandbox' -> SANDBOX.
evidence: src/inspect/logs.ts:7-8 — body: Record<string, unknown> = { query }; if (limit) body.limit = limit. Same pattern for env.
src/lib/flags.ts:5-9 — getFlag(args, '--env') extracts value after --env flag.
src/lib/http.ts:37-41 — hxFetch accepts body: Record<string, unknown> for POST.
ticket.md Override 1 — 'Environment is a plain --env prod|sandbox parameter on the request.'

answers.answer: hlx run should be a top-level command (not hlx inspect run). The server route is POST /api/inspect/:repoId/run (under inspect for auth simplicity), but the CLI command is top-level to reflect the fundamentally different governance model: hlx inspect netsuite is read-only by construction, hlx run allows arbitrary SuiteScript. Top-level placement avoids confusion with the read-only 'inspect' prefix. The handler lives in src/run/index.ts as a new directory.
evidence: RSH-636 AD-1 — Both routes under /api/inspect/ for auth simplicity (server concern).
RSH-636 AD-6 — hlx run allows arbitrary SuiteScript, no assertReadOnlyQuery (different governance).
ticket.md — 'hlx run — arbitrary SuiteScript, not read-only.'
src/index.ts:81-156 — Main dispatcher has dedicated top-level commands for distinct features.

statement: The CLI changes are minimal and pattern-consistent: two new handler files (~20-30 lines each) following the proven resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST -> console.log JSON template, plus two switch-case additions in existing routers. The --env parameter is passed as a body parameter. hlx run is top-level to reflect its distinct governance model. Default environment comes from the manifest's nsDefaultEnv. No new dependencies. No architectural concerns.
